intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street food from local vendors. This bustling market near Tokyo Bay offers an authentic taste of Tokyo's legendary food culture, with dozens of stalls serving everything from grilled seafood to matcha sweets.
experiences.location: Tsukiji, Chuo City (near Tokyo Bay waterfront)

experiences.name: Odaiba Waterfront Tech & Teamlab Borderless
experiences.description: Visit the futuristic man-made island of Odaiba on Tokyo Bay, home to teamLab Borderless digital art museum, the Toyota Mega Web showroom, and cutting-edge tech exhibits. Walk along the beachfront promenade with views of Rainbow Bridge while immersing yourself in Japan's innovation culture.
experiences.location: Odaiba, Minato City (Tokyo Bay beachfront island)

experiences.name: Shinonome & Toyosu Ramen and Izakaya Crawl
experiences.description: Discover the hidden local dining scene near Toyosu and the waterfront districts, hopping between authentic ramen shops, yakitori stalls, and izakayas frequented by locals rather than tourists. Try regional ramen styles and pair them with craft Japanese beers in a relaxed bayside atmosphere.
experiences.location: Toyosu & Shinonome, Koto City (Tokyo Bay area)

experiences.name: Akihabara Electric Town Deep Dive
experiences.description: Spend a day in Akihabara, Tokyo's legendary electronics and otaku district. Browse multi-floor gadget stores, retro game shops, robot cafes, and the latest tech innovations. Visit Yodobashi Camera and smaller specialty shops to experience the heartbeat of Japan's consumer tech culture firsthand.

experiences.name: Toyosu Fish Market Tuna Auction & Sushi Breakfast
experiences.description: Register in advance for the rare opportunity to observe the world-famous tuna auction at Toyosu Market at dawn, then head to the market's upper-floor sushi restaurants for an unforgettable fresh sushi breakfast. This is the ultimate intersection of Tokyo's food heritage and its modern waterfront infrastructure.
experiences.location: Toyosu Market, Koto City (Tokyo Bay waterfront)

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Narita or Haneda Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly Airport Limousine Bus or Keikyu/Narita Express train to Tsukiji area. Check in to your Boutique Stay in Tsukiji, Chuo City. Drop off luggage and freshen up. Take a short orientation walk around the Tsukiji Outer Market neighborhood to get your bearings — explore the narrow lanes, small shops, and street food stalls that are still open in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Tsukiji Outer Market for your first authentic Tokyo dinner. Browse the remaining evening stalls and small restaurants. Try a bowl of ramen or a set meal (teishoku) at one of the local eateries along Shin-Ohashi-dori. Afterward, take a relaxing evening stroll along the Sumida River waterfront nearby.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick onigiri or sandwich from a convenience store (7-Eleven, FamilyMart, or Lawson) near the hotel upon arrival — under ¥500
meals.dinner: Tsukiji Outer Market ramen shop or teishoku restaurant — budget ¥800–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless budget transit throughout the trip. Keep jet lag in mind — don't overdo it on Day 1. Exchange some yen at the airport for convenience.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and visit the Tsukiji Outer Market for a classic Tokyo breakfast experience. Sample fresh tamagoyaki (rolled egg), grilled scallops on a stick, and a bowl of fresh tuna sashimi don at one of the market's affordable breakfast spots. This is one of the best budget food experiences in all of Tokyo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short train ride to Akihabara (Electric Town) — Tokyo's legendary tech and electronics district. Explore multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera and BIC Camera, browse retro game shops, visit Akihabara's famous figure and anime merchandise stores, and check out the free floors of tech arcades. Window-shop the latest gadgets without spending a fortune.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara for dinner and explore the vibrant neon-lit streets at night. Visit a budget-friendly curry rice restaurant or a standing sushi bar (kaiten-zushi). After dinner, explore a multi-floor gaming arcade — many games cost only ¥100 per play.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — tamagoyaki, fresh seafood bites — budget ¥600–¥1,000
meals.lunch: Convenience store bento or a yoshoku (Western-Japanese fusion) lunch set in Akihabara — budget ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: CoCo Ichibanya curry or standing sushi bar in Akihabara — budget ¥800–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is easily reached from Tsukiji via the Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line. Many electronics stores have tax-free counters for tourists — bring your passport. Free Wi-Fi is available at most major stores.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Asakusa, one of Tokyo's most historic and atmospheric neighborhoods. Start at Senso-ji Temple — Tokyo's oldest and most famous Buddhist temple. Explore the Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional snacks like ningyo-yaki (small cakes) and ningyo-yaki. The temple and grounds are completely free to enter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Sumida River toward the Tokyo Skytree area. Browse the Solamachi shopping complex at the base of the Skytree for free (skip the paid observation deck to save budget). Visit the nearby Edo-Tokyo Museum (if open — check current status) or explore the free outdoor areas. Head back toward Nihonbashi or Ginza for a free afternoon walk through Tokyo's historic commercial district.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Tsukiji area for dinner. Try a different spot in the Tsukiji Outer Market — many stalls serve affordable sushi sets, grilled fish, and noodle dishes. Afterward, walk to the Hamarikyu Gardens entrance for a peaceful evening view of the garden lights from outside (entry fee is ¥300 if you want to go inside).

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh melon bread or a morning pastry from a Tsukiji bakery stall — budget ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Ningyo-yaki snacks and a cheap soba set lunch near Asakusa — budget ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Tsukiji Outer Market grilled fish set or sushi — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Asakusa is a short ride from Tsukiji via the Toei Oedo Line or a pleasant walk along the river. April weather may be mild with possible cherry blossom remnants — bring a light jacket. Senso-ji is free to enter at all times.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Harajuku and Omotesando. Start with a free walk down Takeshita Street — the heart of Tokyo's quirky youth fashion and pop culture scene. Browse the colorful boutiques, street fashion shops, and unique accessories. Pick up a famous Harajuku crepe from one of the street stalls for a budget-friendly breakfast treat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down the wide, tree-lined Omotesando Boulevard — Tokyo's answer to the Champs-Élysées. Window-shop the designer stores for free and admire the architecture. Then head to the nearby Meiji Jingu Shrine (free entry) — a serene forested Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji, offering a peaceful contrast to the busy shopping streets.
day_by_day.evening: Make your way to Shibuya for the evening. Experience the world-famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing — one of the busiest pedestrian intersections on Earth. Explore the surrounding area and streets. Grab dinner at one of Shibuya's many affordable ramen shops, gyudon (beef bowl) chains like Yoshinoya or Matsuya, or a conveyor belt sushi restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Harajuku crepe from a Takeshita Street stall — budget ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Budget ramen or udon near Harajuku/Omotesando — budget ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Gyudon at Yoshinoya or Matsuya in Shibuya, or conveyor belt sushi — budget ¥500–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Harajuku is best visited on weekends when the street fashion scene is most vibrant. The Meiji Jingu forest walk is a wonderful free experience. Use the JR Yamanote Line to connect between Harajuku and Shibuya — just one stop.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island in Tokyo Bay. Take the free Yurikamome automated monorail (or the Rinkai Line) to get there. Walk along the Odaiba waterfront for stunning views of the Rainbow Bridge and the Tokyo skyline. Explore the free outdoor areas and the replica Statue of Liberty.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets digital art museum (pre-book online for discounts — around ¥3,200). This is a world-class immersive tech-art experience that perfectly aligns with your tech culture interest. Alternatively, visit the free DiverCity Tokyo Plaza to see the life-size Unicorn Gundam statue — a must-see for tech and anime fans. Browse the free floors of Aqua City Odaiba mall.
day_by_day.evening: Take the scenic Yurikamome monorail back toward central Tokyo, enjoying the nighttime views of the illuminated Rainbow Bridge. Head to Shimbashi or Ginza for a budget ramen or izakaya dinner. Explore the Ginza area at night — window shopping is completely free.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near the hotel — onigiri, coffee, and a pastry — budget ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Food court meal at DiverCity Tokyo Plaza or a convenience store bento — budget ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Ramen shop or izakaya near Shimbashi — budget ¥800–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: teamLab museums require advance booking — check availability and book online before the trip. The Unicorn Gundam statue at DiverCity is free to view and is a spectacular sight. Odaiba is a great place to experience Tokyo's vision of the future.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Ueno — Tokyo's cultural and museum hub. Visit Ueno Park (free entry) and stroll through the park, which may still have late cherry blossoms in mid-April. Visit the Tokyo National Museum's main building (¥1,000 general admission) — Japan's largest museum with thousands of artifacts spanning Japanese history, art, and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ameyoko Market — a lively open-air street market stretching under the JR train tracks near Ueno Station. Browse stalls selling fresh food, dried seafood, spices, clothing, and electronics at bargain prices. This is a fantastic budget food and shopping experience. Try some street snacks as you walk.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Akihabara for a second visit focused on the tech culture side — visit the free floors of multi-story electronics stores, explore the retro game shops for used bargains, and consider visiting a maid café for a uniquely Tokyo cultural experience (budget around ¥1,000–¥1,500 for a drink and entry). Dinner at a nearby budget restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast or a local kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) near the hotel — budget ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Street food from Ameyoko Market — grilled skewers, fresh fruit, or a rice ball — budget ¥500–¥800
meals.dinner: Tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) set or ramen near Akihabara — budget ¥800–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Ueno Park is free to enter. The Tokyo National Museum is one of the best value cultural experiences in the city. Ameyoko Market is busiest in the afternoon — great for budget food finds. Monday is generally less crowded at most attractions.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old downtown (shitamachi) neighborhoods. Explore the charming Yanaka Ginza shopping street, browse independent craft shops, traditional sweets stores, and local galleries. The area has a wonderfully authentic, unhurried atmosphere that feels like old Tokyo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Yanaka Cemetery (free, peaceful, and historically significant) and the surrounding Nezu and Yanesen neighborhoods. Visit the Nezu Shrine (free entry) — a smaller but beautiful Shinto shrine with a row of torii gates similar to Fushimi Inari in Kyoto. Browse the narrow backstreets and local cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo via the JR Yamanote Line. Head to Shibuya or Shinjuku for the evening. Explore the free observation deck at the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building in Shinjuku (free, open until 22:30 on most nights) for a spectacular panoramic night view of the entire Tokyo skyline.

meals.breakfast: Grab onigiri and coffee from a convenience store near the hotel — budget ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Yanaka Ginza street food — grilled mochi, croquettes, or a set lunch at a local diner — budget ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Ramen, gyoza, or a budget izakaya near Shinjuku station — budget ¥800–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is completely free — one of the best budget-friendly views in Tokyo. Yanaka is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. The Nezu Shrine is far less crowded than Senso-ji and equally beautiful.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shibuya in the morning when it's less crowded. Explore the Shibuya Stream and Shibuya Scramble Square areas. Check out the free observation terrace at Shibuya Sky (or pay ¥2,000 for the rooftop — worth it for the view). Browse the free floors of Shibuya 109 and the surrounding youth fashion district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Shimokitazawa — a bohemian, artsy neighborhood known for its vintage clothing shops, independent music venues, and café culture. Browse the many secondhand and vintage clothing shops for unique budget fashion finds. Explore the narrow, winding streets and discover independent bookshops and record stores.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the local live music scene in Shimokitazawa — many small live houses have affordable cover charges (¥1,000–¥2,000). Alternatively, head back to Shinjuku's Kabukicho area for a free evening walk through Tokyo's most famous entertainment district. Grab dinner at a budget ramen shop or a standing bar (tachinomi) for an authentic local experience.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and toast at a local kissaten in Shibuya — budget ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Curry rice or a budget lunch set in Shimokitazawa — budget ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Ramen or yakitori skewers at a local izakaya in Shimokitazawa or Shinjuku — budget ¥800–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Shimokitazawa is Tokyo's hidden gem for budget travelers interested in culture and local life. The vintage shops offer excellent value. Use the Odakyu Line from Shinjuku to reach Shimokitazawa — just two stops.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Koenji — another fantastic neighborhood for local food and alternative culture. Browse the covered shopping arcades (shotengai) and the many vintage and secondhand shops. Koenji has a strong local music and arts scene and is far less touristy than Shibuya or Harajuku.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Nakano Broadway complex — a multi-story shopping center famous for its massive collection of vintage anime figures, manga, retro games, and tech collectibles. This is a paradise for tech culture enthusiasts and often more affordable than Akihabara. Spend the afternoon browsing the many Mandarake shops inside.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Tsukiji area for a special dinner. Try a sit-down sushi restaurant in the Tsukiji Outer Market area — many offer affordable omakase-style sets or sashimi platters at reasonable prices compared to upscale sushi restaurants elsewhere. This is a great mid-trip treat on a budget.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast or a local bakery near the hotel — budget ¥300–¥600
meals.lunch: Local ramen or udon shop in Koenji — budget ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Affordable sushi set or sashimi don at a Tsukiji area restaurant — budget ¥1,200–¥2,000

day_by_day.notes: Koenji and Nakano are both on the JR Chuo/Sobu Line — easy to combine in one day. Nakano Broadway's Mandarake stores are a must-visit for tech and pop culture enthusiasts. Prices at Tsukiji sushi restaurants are generally much more reasonable than in tourist-heavy areas.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Kawagoe (Little Edo) — a historic town about 40 minutes from Shinjuku by the Seibu Shinjuku Line or Tobu Tojo Line (budget ¥500–¥700 round trip). Explore the beautifully preserved Edo-period warehouse district (Kurazukuri Street) with its iconic black-walled merchant buildings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Kawagoe — visit the Toki no Kane (Bell of Time) tower, browse the Kashiya Yokocho (Candy Alley) for traditional Japanese sweets and snacks at very affordable prices, and explore the local temples and shrines. This is a wonderful escape from the urban intensity of Tokyo.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Head to the Nihonbashi or Ginza area — both close to your Tsukiji hotel. Take a free evening walk along Chuo-dori and explore the historic Nihonbashi bridge area. Grab a budget-friendly dinner at a local soba restaurant or a standing ramen bar.

meals.breakfast: Grab onigiri and a drink from a convenience store before catching the train — budget ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Traditional unagi (eel) rice or a local set lunch in Kawagoe — budget ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Soba or ramen near Nihonbashi or Tsukiji — budget ¥700–¥1,000

day_by_day.notes: Kawagoe is an excellent and affordable day trip from Tokyo. The Candy Alley is a fun and very cheap experience — most snacks cost ¥50–¥200. Check train schedules in advance using the Hyperdia or Google Maps app.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Toyosu Market (the relocated Tsukiji wholesale fish market) — take the Yurikamome monorail from Shimbashi. The inner wholesale tuna auction viewing area requires advance booking (free but limited), but the outer market area with restaurants and observation areas is accessible without a reservation. Experience the world's largest fish market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Roppongi — Tokyo's international arts district. Visit the Mori Art Museum (¥1,800 — includes access to the Tokyo City View observation deck, making it excellent value). The museum frequently features cutting-edge contemporary and tech-inspired art exhibitions. The observation deck offers panoramic views of Tokyo.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Roppongi Hills and the surrounding area at night — the complex is beautiful after dark. Walk to the nearby Azabu-Juban neighborhood for a more local, less touristy dinner experience. Try one of the many affordable Japanese restaurants on the main shopping street.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at a Toyosu Market restaurant — fresh sushi or seafood don — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.lunch: Convenience store or a quick bite near Roppongi — budget ¥600–¥900
meals.dinner: Local izakaya or ramen shop in Azabu-Juban — budget ¥800–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Toyosu Market tuna auction viewing requires advance online lottery registration — check the Tokyo Metropolitan Central Wholesale Market website well in advance. The Mori Art Museum is one of Tokyo's best contemporary art venues and the combined ticket with the observation deck is great value.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300 entry — excellent value) — a beautiful traditional Japanese garden right next to your Tsukiji hotel. Enjoy a peaceful morning walk through the garden's tidal ponds, tea house (matcha tea available for around ¥500), and seasonal flowers. This is one of Tokyo's most underrated gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the water bus (Tokyo Cruise) from Hamarikyu Gardens pier to Asakusa (¥780) — a scenic and budget-friendly boat ride along the Sumida River. Arrive in Asakusa for a final afternoon of souvenir shopping at Nakamise-dori. Pick up budget-friendly gifts like tenugui (hand towels), Japanese snacks, and traditional crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Final major dinner in Tokyo — treat yourself to a slightly nicer budget experience. Visit a conveyor belt sushi restaurant (kaiten-zushi) like Sushiro or Kura Sushi for high-quality sushi at ¥110–¥165 per plate. Spend the evening doing a final walk through the Tsukiji Outer Market and the surrounding Chuo City streets to soak in the atmosphere one last time.

meals.breakfast: Matcha tea and traditional wagashi sweets inside Hamarikyu Gardens — budget ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Street food at Asakusa Nakamise-dori — ningyo-yaki, senbei crackers, and melonpan — budget ¥500–¥800
meals.dinner: Kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt sushi) near Tsukiji — budget ¥1,200–¥2,000

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo Cruise water bus is a wonderful and affordable way to see the city from the water. Book Hamarikyu to Asakusa tickets at the pier. The Hamarikyu Gardens are a hidden gem just steps from your hotel — perfect for a relaxed penultimate day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo. Wake up early for one last visit to the Tsukiji Outer Market for a farewell breakfast — enjoy fresh tamagoyaki, grilled seafood, and a bowl of clam miso soup. Browse any remaining market stalls for last-minute food souvenirs like dried seaweed, bonito flakes, or Japanese condiments.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, use the remaining time to revisit a favorite neighborhood, pick up any last souvenirs from a 100-yen shop (Daiso or Seria — excellent for budget gifts), or simply relax near the hotel. Check out of the hotel and store luggage at the front desk if needed. Head to the airport via the Airport Limousine Bus or train with plenty of time to spare.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Tokyo. Reflect on 13 incredible days of local food, tech culture, and authentic Tokyo experiences.

meals.breakfast: Final Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — fresh seafood, tamagoyaki, miso soup — budget ¥800–¥1,200
meals.lunch: Airport terminal food — try a quick soba or udon at one of the airport restaurants — budget ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: On the plane or at the airport

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Narita, or 2 hours for Haneda. Use your remaining Suica card balance at convenience stores or vending machines before departure — or keep the card for a future trip (¥500 deposit is refundable at the airport). Pack any purchased food items carefully to comply with customs regulations.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and transit from airport to hotel in Tsukiji, Chuo City. Check-in and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Tsukiji Outer Market on foot. Browse the stalls selling fresh seafood snacks, tamagoyaki (rolled omelette), and local street food. Get oriented with the neighborhood and pick up any essentials at a nearby convenience store.
day_by_day.evening: Easy first evening stroll along the Sumida River waterfront. Visit Hamarikyu Gardens (open until 17:00, so aim to arrive by 15:30 if energy allows) or simply walk the scenic riverside promenade near the hotel. Wind down early to recover from jet lag.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab an onigiri and green tea at a 7-Eleven or FamilyMart near the hotel upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a light snack at Tsukiji Outer Market — try fresh tuna sashimi on rice (kaisendon) from one of the market stalls for around ¥1,200–¥1,800.
meals.dinner: Sushi Zanmai Tsukiji (main branch) — a beloved mid-range sushi chain steps from the hotel. Set menus from ¥2,000–¥3,500. Perfect introduction to Tokyo sushi culture.

day_by_day.notes: Priority on Day 1 is settling in and gentle acclimatization. Don't over-schedule. Tsukiji Outer Market stalls begin closing around 14:00–15:00, so head there promptly after check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Tsukiji Outer Market (7:00–9:00) to experience it at peak freshness. Sample grilled scallops, fresh oysters, and tamagoyaki from different vendors. This is the quintessential Tokyo food experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Akihabara (Electric Town) by subway — 15 minutes from Tsukiji. Immerse yourself in Tokyo's legendary tech and electronics culture: browse multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera and Akihabara Radio Center, explore retro game shops, and visit the iconic Akihabara UDX building.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara for dinner and evening exploration. Visit a maid café for a uniquely Japanese pop-culture experience, then browse the illuminated storefronts and arcades.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market street food — fresh seafood skewers, tamagoyaki, and green tea. Budget ¥800–¥1,500.
meals.lunch: Ramen at Fuunji or a nearby tonkotsu ramen shop in Akihabara. Budget ¥900–¥1,300.
meals.dinner: Kanda Yabu Soba near Akihabara — a historic soba restaurant dating to 1880. Soba sets ¥1,200–¥2,500. Alternatively, try a yakiniku (grilled meat) restaurant in the area for ¥2,500–¥4,000.

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is a must for tech culture enthusiasts. The area is best explored on foot. IC card (Suica/Pasmo) is essential for subway travel — load it at the airport or at any station.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa (opens at sunrise). Arrive by 8:00–9:00 to beat the crowds. Walk Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional souvenirs — ningyo-yaki cakes, tenugui towels, and chopsticks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center observation deck (free) for panoramic views. Then walk to the nearby Kappabashi Kitchenware Street — a fascinating street lined with professional kitchen supply shops and the famous plastic food replica stores, deeply tied to Japanese food culture.
day_by_day.evening: Cruise on a Sumida River water bus (Tokyo Cruise) from Asakusa Pier back toward Hinode Pier near Tsukiji — scenic and relaxing. Tickets around ¥780–¥1,200.

meals.breakfast: Asakusa Imahan or a local kissaten (retro Japanese coffee shop) near Senso-ji for a morning set — coffee, toast, and egg for ¥600–¥900.
meals.lunch: Tempura Daikokuya in Asakusa — a legendary tempura-don restaurant since 1887. Tempura rice bowls ¥1,800–¥2,800.
meals.dinner: Izakaya dinner near Tsukiji or Ginza — try Torikizoku or a local neighborhood izakaya for yakitori skewers, edamame, and cold Asahi beer. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday means Asakusa will be busy by mid-morning. Arrive early for the best experience. The Sumida River cruise is a relaxing way to return to the hotel area.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Ginza, Tokyo's upscale shopping and design district, a short walk from the hotel. Visit the iconic Itoya stationery store (9 floors of Japanese stationery and design), the Sony Park, and browse the architecture of flagship brand stores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the teamLab Borderless digital art museum (book tickets in advance online — ¥3,200). This world-famous immersive tech-art installation is a perfect intersection of technology and culture. Located in Azabudai Hills, accessible by subway.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ginza for an evening walk — the district is beautifully lit at night. Browse the Ginza Six mall's rooftop garden and lower-level food hall.

meals.breakfast: Café de l'Ambre in Ginza — a legendary old-school coffee shop open since 1948. Coffee from ¥700.
meals.lunch: Ginza Six basement food hall — pick from a curated selection of Japanese bento boxes, sushi, and prepared foods. Budget ¥1,200–¥2,000.
meals.dinner: Kyubey Ginza — a respected mid-range sushi restaurant in Ginza. Omakase lunch-style dinner sets from ¥5,000–¥8,000. Splurge-worthy for a special evening.

day_by_day.notes: Book teamLab Borderless tickets at least 1–2 weeks in advance online. Sunday can be busy. Ginza is walkable from the Tsukiji hotel — approximately 10 minutes on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic waterfront island. Take the Yurikamome automated driverless monorail from Shimbashi Station for a scenic ride over Rainbow Bridge. Visit the teamLab Planets (different from Borderless — book separately, ¥3,200) or the Toyota Mega Web automotive showcase (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore DiverCity Tokyo Plaza and the giant life-size Gundam statue outside. Browse the Palette Town shopping complex and visit the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation (Miraikan) — a world-class science and tech museum with robots and interactive exhibits. Entry ¥630.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset over Tokyo Bay from Odaiba's beach promenade with Rainbow Bridge and the city skyline as backdrop. Return to Tsukiji via Yurikamome or water bus.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near the hotel — onigiri, tamagoyaki sandwich, and canned coffee. Budget ¥400–¥700.
meals.lunch: Decks Tokyo Beach food floor in Odaiba — multiple options including ramen, curry, and seafood. Budget ¥1,200–¥1,800.
meals.dinner: Tsukiji neighborhood dinner — try Sushi Bun or a local seafood izakaya near the hotel. Budget ¥2,500–¥4,000.

day_by_day.notes: Odaiba is a full-day destination. Miraikan is closed on Tuesdays. The Yurikamome monorail ride itself is a highlight — sit at the front for the best views.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shibuya — take the subway to Shibuya Station. Visit the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing (best viewed from the Starbucks or Mag's Park observation area above). Walk to Shibuya Sky observation deck (¥2,000, book online) for 360° city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from Shibuya to Harajuku (15 minutes on foot). Explore Takeshita Street for youth fashion and crepe culture, then stroll the quieter Omotesando boulevard — Tokyo's Champs-Élysées — lined with flagship stores and stunning architecture by Tadao Ando and others.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Omotesando Hills mall's stunning interior, then head to a rooftop bar in Shibuya or Omotesando for cocktails with city views.

meals.breakfast: Ichiran Ramen Shibuya (24-hour) for a solo-booth tonkotsu ramen experience — a tech-forward ordering system with individual booths. ¥980–¥1,500.
meals.lunch: Gyukatsu Motomura in Shibuya — beef katsu (breaded beef cutlet) cooked on a personal tabletop grill. ¥1,500–¥2,200.
meals.dinner: Udon Shin in Omotesando — creative, high-quality udon in a minimalist setting. ¥1,200–¥2,000. Or explore the Omotesando Hills basement food options.

day_by_day.notes: Shibuya Scramble is most dramatic in the evening when the crossing is illuminated. Consider returning after dinner for night photos.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shinjuku — Tokyo's busiest district. Start at the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (free, opens 9:30) for panoramic views including Mt. Fuji on clear days. Explore the surrounding Shinjuku Nishi-guchi (West Exit) skyscraper district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross to Shinjuku East Side — explore Kabukicho entertainment district by day (safe and fascinating to walk), then visit the Golden Gai alley network — a labyrinth of tiny bars and eateries that perfectly captures old Tokyo atmosphere. Browse Isetan department store's legendary basement food hall (depachika).
day_by_day.evening: Experience Shinjuku's famous nightlife district — drinks at a Golden Gai bar (most bars welcome tourists, cover charge ¥500–¥1,000, drinks ¥600–¥1,200) for an intimate, one-of-a-kind Tokyo experience.

meals.breakfast: Tsukemen (dipping ramen) at Fuunji Shinjuku — one of Tokyo's most acclaimed ramen shops. Opens at 11:00, so have a light hotel breakfast first. ¥950–¥1,300.
meals.lunch: Isetan B1 depachika — pick up artisanal Japanese foods, premium onigiri, and wagashi sweets. Budget ¥1,000–¥2,000.
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — a narrow alley of tiny yakitori stalls near Shinjuku Station West Exit. Smoky, atmospheric, and delicious. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,500 including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku is overwhelming in the best way. Wear comfortable shoes. Golden Gai bars are tiny (some seat only 5–8 people) — embrace the intimacy.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (2 hours by Tobu Nikko Limited Express from Asakusa Station, ¥2,720 each way). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine complex — ornate, gold-leafed mausoleums set in ancient cedar forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko: walk to Rinno-ji Temple and Futarasan Shrine. Hike up to Kegon Waterfall (one of Japan's three great waterfalls) via elevator (¥570). Enjoy the mountain air and spring foliage.
day_by_day.evening: Return train to Tokyo. Arrive back at Tsukiji by 20:00–21:00. Light dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before departing for Asakusa Station.
meals.lunch: Nikko Yuba (tofu skin) cuisine at a restaurant near the shrine complex — a local specialty. Set lunch ¥1,500–¥2,500.
meals.dinner: Kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt sushi) near Tsukiji or Ginza upon return — Uobei or Hamazushi for budget-friendly sushi. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.

day_by_day.notes: Buy the Tobu Nikko All Area Pass (¥4,780) for unlimited buses within Nikko — worth it for the day. Depart Asakusa by 8:00–9:00 to maximize time in Nikko.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old downtown (shitamachi) neighborhoods. Walk the Yanaka Ginza shopping street for local snacks, traditional crafts, and a glimpse of pre-war Tokyo atmosphere. Visit Yanaka Cemetery for a peaceful stroll among cherry blossom trees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to nearby Nezu Shrine — a beautiful, less-crowded alternative to Fushimi Inari with its own tunnel of torii gates. Then visit the Nezu Museum in Omotesando for Japanese and East Asian art in a stunning garden setting (¥1,300).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ueno for the evening — explore Ameyoko Market for street food and shopping before stalls close around 19:00–20:00.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka Ginza street food — menchi-katsu (fried meat patty), croquettes, and local sweets from vendor stalls. Budget ¥600–¥1,000.
meals.lunch: Hantei in Yanaka — a beautifully preserved 100-year-old wooden townhouse serving kushiage (deep-fried skewers on sticks) in a multi-course format. ¥2,800–¥4,000.
meals.dinner: Ameyoko Market area — try Korean-Japanese fusion at one of the lively restaurants, or grab grilled seafood from Ameyoko stalls. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored slowly on foot. The neighborhood has a rare, authentic old-Tokyo feel that contrasts beautifully with the city's modern face. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno (¥1,000) — Japan's largest and oldest museum, housing an extraordinary collection of samurai armor, ceramics, woodblock prints, and Buddhist art. Spend 2–3 hours exploring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ueno Park — visit the Tokyo Metropolitan Art Museum and stroll the park's ponds and paths. Then take the subway to Akihabara for a second, deeper dive: visit the Akihabara Radio Center (vintage electronics), retro game shops, and the 8-floor Super Potato retro game store.
day_by_day.evening: Akihabara at night — the neon-lit streets are spectacular after dark. Visit an arcade (game center) for UFO catcher machines, rhythm games, and photo booths (purikura).

meals.breakfast: Ueno Seiyoken — a historic Western-style restaurant in Ueno Park open since 1876. Morning set ¥1,200–¥1,800.
meals.lunch: Curry at a Japanese curry chain (CoCo Ichibanya) near Ueno or Akihabara — customizable spice levels and toppings. ¥900–¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Akihabara's Gundam Café or a themed restaurant for fun, or a solid ramen shop in the area. Budget ¥1,200–¥2,000.

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo National Museum requires a full morning to appreciate properly. Audio guides are available in English. Akihabara on a Saturday evening is buzzing with energy.

day_by_day.morning: Half-day trip to Kawagoe (Little Edo) — 1 hour from Shinjuku by Seibu-Shinjuku Line (¥530). Explore the preserved Edo-period warehouse district (kurazukuri) with its distinctive black-walled merchant buildings. Visit the famous Bell Tower and sweet potato snack street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Tokyo by 14:00. Visit Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300) — a stunning traditional Japanese garden adjacent to the hotel in Tsukiji, with a teahouse on a tidal pond where you can enjoy matcha and wagashi sweets.
day_by_day.evening: Leisurely evening in the Tsukiji/Ginza neighborhood. Browse the Ginza Six rooftop garden at sunset, then enjoy a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before departing for Kawagoe.
meals.lunch: Kawagoe's Kurazukuri Honpo — try imo (sweet potato) dishes, a Kawagoe specialty. Unaju (eel over rice) is also famous here. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.
meals.dinner: Hamarikyu Teahouse for matcha (¥710 including tea and wagashi) as a late-afternoon snack, then dinner at a neighborhood sushi-ya near Tsukiji. Budget ¥3,000–¥5,000.

day_by_day.notes: Kawagoe is a refreshing half-day escape from the city. The kurazukuri district is most photogenic in the morning light. Return early to enjoy the Hamarikyu Gardens before closing time (17:00).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Roppongi — start at the Mori Art Museum (¥2,000) on the 53rd floor of Mori Tower, featuring contemporary art exhibitions and a sky-high observation deck with 360° Tokyo views. A perfect blend of art and technology.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the National Art Center Tokyo in Roppongi (free admission to permanent collection areas, ¥1,500 for special exhibitions) — Japan's largest exhibition space with a stunning wave-glass facade designed by Kisho Kurokawa. Then walk to Roppongi Hills for the outdoor sculpture garden.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Tokyo — make it special. Head to a rooftop bar in Roppongi or return to Ginza for a memorable farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a kissaten (Japanese coffee shop) near Tsukiji for morning coffee and toast set. Budget ¥600–¥1,000.
meals.lunch: Roppongi Hills food floor — diverse options from Japanese to international cuisine. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.
meals.dinner: Splurge farewell dinner: Sushi Saito (if reservations possible — extremely exclusive) or more accessible Sushi Yoshitake in Ginza for an omakase experience. Alternatively, Narisawa in Minami-Aoyama for innovative Japanese cuisine. Budget ¥8,000–¥15,000 for a special send-off.

day_by_day.notes: Book the farewell dinner restaurant well in advance — top Tokyo restaurants fill up weeks or months ahead. The Mori Art Museum is open until 22:00 on most days, making it a great evening option if preferred.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tsukiji — one last walk through the Outer Market for breakfast and souvenirs. Pick up vacuum-packed dashi packs, wasabi, nori, and Japanese kitchen tools to bring home. Visit any remaining spots in the Ginza/Tsukiji neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack, check out of the hotel, and store luggage at the hotel or at a coin locker at the nearest station. Make a final visit to any missed spots or do last-minute shopping at Don Quijote (Donki) in Ginza for affordable Japanese snacks, cosmetics, and electronics.
day_by_day.evening: Depart for the airport (Narita: ~60 min by Narita Express from Tokyo Station; Haneda: ~30 min by monorail). Allow 2.5–3 hours before international departure.

meals.breakfast: Final Tsukiji Outer Market feast — fresh uni (sea urchin) on rice, grilled oysters, and tamagoyaki. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500. Savor every bite.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel or airport — katsu sandwich from a convenience store or airport ramen. Budget ¥800–¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Airport dinner at Narita or Haneda — both airports have excellent restaurant floors with authentic ramen, sushi, and tempura. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.

day_by_day.notes: Coin lockers are available at Tokyo Station and most major stations — useful for storing bags on the last day. Don Quijote in Ginza offers tax-free shopping for tourists (passport required). Leave enough transit time for the airport — Tokyo traffic can be unpredictable.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street food from local vendors. This bustling market near Tokyo Bay offers an authentic taste of Tokyo's legendary food culture, with dozens of stalls serving everything from grilled seafood to matcha sweets.
experiences.location: Tsukiji, Chuo City (near Tokyo Bay waterfront)

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Narita/Haneda Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport to boutique hotel in Tsukiji, Chuo City. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your premium suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk around the Tsukiji Outer Market neighborhood. Browse the iconic stalls, absorb the vibrant atmosphere, pick up light snacks such as freshly grilled taiyaki and matcha soft-serve, and get your bearings in the area. Visit the nearby Namiyoke Inari Shrine for a calm, reflective start to the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive dinner at Sushi Saito (or equivalent Michelin-starred omakase counter in Chuo City) — a multi-course omakase experience featuring the finest seasonal nigiri and sashimi. Book the chef's counter for a deeply personal, premium introduction to Tokyo's world-class sushi culture.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal or airport lounge dining before arrival
meals.lunch: Light street snacks at Tsukiji Outer Market stalls — grilled scallops, tamagoyaki skewers, and fresh oysters
meals.dinner: Omakase dinner at a Michelin-starred sushi counter in Chuo City (approx. ¥30,000–¥50,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag is likely after a long-haul Lufthansa flight. Keep Day 1 light and relaxed. Confirm omakase reservation well in advance — top Tokyo sushi counters book out months ahead. Private airport transfer recommended for comfort.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — join a premium guided experience exploring the market's legendary stalls. Sample fresh sushi, house-made tamagoyaki, sea urchin, and rare seasonal seafood. Engage with veteran vendors and learn the history of one of the world's most famous food markets. Pair with a traditional Japanese breakfast set at a market-adjacent teahouse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ginza (10 minutes from Tsukiji) for an afternoon of luxury retail and cultural exploration. Visit the flagship Apple Ginza store — one of Asia's most architecturally striking tech retail spaces. Explore the Sony Park concept space and the Itoya flagship stationery store. Browse Ginza Six's curated designer boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten (Jiro Dreams of Sushi) or equivalent legendary sushi institution in Ginza. Alternatively, enjoy a premium teppanyaki experience at Ginza Ukai-tei, where theatrical cooking meets world-class Wagyu beef.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast set (grilled fish, miso soup, pickles, rice) at a Tsukiji market teahouse
meals.lunch: Gourmet market lunch — fresh uni don (sea urchin rice bowl) at a top-rated Tsukiji stall
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred sushi or teppanyaki in Ginza (approx. ¥25,000–¥60,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Tsukiji Outer Market food tour is best experienced before 10:00 AM when stalls are freshest and least crowded. Book a premium guided tour for VIP access and deeper storytelling. Ginza is a 5-minute taxi ride or pleasant walk from Tsukiji.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Akihabara — Tokyo's legendary Electric Town and global hub of tech culture, anime, and electronics. Explore multi-story electronics megastores (Yodobashi Camera, Sofmap), discover cutting-edge gadgets, retro gaming arcades, and futuristic robotics demonstrations. Visit the Akihabara Radio Kaikan building for rare tech collectibles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Akihabara — experience a high-tech maid café for cultural immersion, visit the Gundam Café, and explore the underground world of Japan's otaku culture. Head to the nearby 3331 Arts Chiyoda for contemporary digital art and tech-art crossover exhibitions.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo. Dinner at a premium Kaiseki restaurant in Nihonbashi (adjacent to Tsukiji) — a multi-course traditional Japanese haute cuisine experience showcasing seasonal ingredients, artistic plating, and centuries-old culinary philosophy. Ryugin or Nihonbashi Yukari are excellent options.

meals.breakfast: Western-Japanese fusion breakfast at the hotel or a premium café in Tsukiji
meals.lunch: Ramen at a celebrated Akihabara ramen shop — try a rich tonkotsu or shoyu broth at a top-rated counter
meals.dinner: Kaiseki multi-course dinner in Nihonbashi (approx. ¥20,000–¥40,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is approximately 20 minutes from Tsukiji by subway (Hibiya Line to Akihabara). Friday afternoons can be busy — arrive early for the best experience. Bring a small bag for electronics purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Visit TeamLab Planets in Toyosu (15 minutes from Tsukiji) — an immersive, world-renowned digital art museum where technology and nature converge. Walk through stunning rooms of infinite light, floating flowers, and mirrored water installations. Book the first entry slot for a quieter, more intimate experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Toyosu Market — the modern successor to Tsukiji's wholesale operations. Book a premium observation tour to witness the world's most sophisticated seafood auction and distribution systems. Then visit the Toyosu Smart City development, a showcase of Japan's urban tech innovation.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium seafood restaurant overlooking Tokyo Bay in the Toyosu or Shinonome area. Alternatively, take a short trip to Odaiba for dinner at a waterfront restaurant with panoramic views of the Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo skyline.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or artisan coffee and pastries at a specialty café near Tsukiji
meals.lunch: Premium sashimi set at a Toyosu Market-adjacent restaurant featuring ultra-fresh auction-grade fish
meals.dinner: Waterfront seafood kaiseki or French-Japanese fusion dinner (approx. ¥18,000–¥35,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: TeamLab Planets advance booking is essential — tickets sell out weeks ahead, especially on weekends. Toyosu Market observation tours must be reserved through the official Tokyo Metropolitan Central Wholesale Market website. Wear comfortable shoes for TeamLab as guests walk barefoot through water installations.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the historic Hamarikyu Gardens (10 minutes from Tsukiji) — a stunning traditional Japanese landscape garden with a tidal pond, teahouse, and seasonal cherry blossom or wisteria blooms in April. Enjoy a formal matcha tea ceremony in the garden's 300-year-old Nakajima-no-Ochaya teahouse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board a luxury Sumida River cruise from Hamarikyu to Asakusa — glide past historic bridges and Tokyo's evolving skyline. Explore Asakusa's Senso-ji Temple complex, Nakamise shopping street (premium crafts and wagashi sweets), and the Kappabashi kitchen district for artisan culinary tools.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Asakusa at Komagata Dojo — a historic 200-year-old restaurant specializing in loach (dojo) hot pot, a traditional Edo-period delicacy. Alternatively, dine at a premium tempura counter such as Tempura Daikokuya for a refined take on this beloved Tokyo specialty.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Wagashi (traditional Japanese sweets) and matcha in Asakusa, followed by a premium bento at a Nakamise tea shop
meals.dinner: Historic Edo-style dinner in Asakusa (approx. ¥10,000–¥20,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: April is peak cherry blossom season — Hamarikyu Gardens may have stunning late blooms or wisteria. The Sumida River cruise is a scenic and relaxing transit option (approx. 40 minutes). Book the tea ceremony in advance for a private session.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shibuya — start at the iconic Shibuya Scramble Crossing, then head to the Shibuya Sky observation deck for 360-degree panoramic views of Tokyo. Explore Shibuya Stream and Shibuya Scramble Square, architectural landmarks of Tokyo's tech-driven urban redevelopment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tech culture deep-dive in Shibuya — visit the Google Japan office area in Roppongi Hills (short taxi ride), explore the Mori Digital Art Museum, and browse Bic Camera's flagship tech floors. Discover cutting-edge wearable tech and robotics at specialty stores in the Shibuya/Harajuku corridor.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Florilège in Shibuya — a celebrated two-Michelin-star French-Japanese restaurant known for boundary-pushing cuisine using local Japanese ingredients. One of Tokyo's most exciting fine dining experiences.

meals.breakfast: Artisan coffee and fresh croissants at a premium Shibuya café (e.g., Fuglen Tokyo or Blue Bottle Coffee Shibuya)
meals.lunch: Premium soba at a high-end Shibuya soba restaurant — try hand-cut Shinshu soba with seasonal tempura
meals.dinner: Two-Michelin-star French-Japanese cuisine at Florilège (approx. ¥25,000–¥40,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Shibuya is approximately 30 minutes from Tsukiji by subway. The Shibuya Sky observation deck is best visited at sunset for dramatic city views — book timed entry tickets online. Florilège requires advance reservation; book at least 2–3 months ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island. Visit the teamLab borderless digital art museum (if not visited previously), the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation (Miraikan), and the life-size 18-meter Unicorn Gundam statue. Explore Palette Town and the iconic Venus Fort shopping complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Toyota Mega Web showroom in Odaiba — an extraordinary interactive automotive and technology exhibition featuring concept cars, autonomous driving demos, and a history of Japanese automotive innovation. Continue to the Fuji TV Building observation deck for panoramic bay views.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner cruise on Tokyo Bay — board a premium yakatabune (traditional pleasure boat) for a multi-course Japanese dinner while gliding beneath the Rainbow Bridge with views of the glittering Tokyo skyline. A uniquely romantic and culturally rich evening experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store premium breakfast (7-Eleven Japan's gourmet offerings are a cultural experience in themselves)
meals.lunch: Ramen or gyoza at a popular Odaiba food court, or a premium burger at a Japanese craft burger restaurant
meals.dinner: Multi-course dinner on a luxury yakatabune cruise on Tokyo Bay (approx. ¥15,000–¥25,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Odaiba is accessible via the Yurikamome automated monorail from Shimbashi (25 minutes from Tsukiji). The driverless monorail ride itself is a tech-culture highlight. Book the yakatabune cruise well in advance as they are popular with both tourists and locals.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Roppongi — visit the Mori Art Museum at the top of Roppongi Hills for world-class contemporary art and technology-themed exhibitions. Access the Tokyo City View observation deck for stunning morning cityscape photography. The 52-story Roppongi Hills complex is itself a masterpiece of urban design.
day_by_day.afternoon: Discover the National Art Center Tokyo in Roppongi — Japan's largest exhibition space, architecturally stunning with a dramatic wave-glass facade. Visit the 21_21 Design Sight museum in Midtown Tokyo, founded by legendary designer Issey Miyake, for cutting-edge design and tech exhibitions.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Ryugin in Roppongi — one of Japan's most celebrated three-Michelin-star kaiseki restaurants, where Chef Seiji Yamamoto reinterprets ancient Japanese culinary traditions through a modern, scientific lens. An unmissable experience for food and tech culture enthusiasts alike.

meals.breakfast: Japanese breakfast set at the hotel or a premium Roppongi café
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at the Mori Art Museum café with panoramic city views, or a premium bento at a Roppongi Hills restaurant
meals.dinner: Three-Michelin-star kaiseki at Ryugin (approx. ¥40,000–¥60,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Roppongi is 20 minutes from Tsukiji by taxi. The Mori Art Museum frequently hosts technology and digital culture exhibitions — check the current program before visiting. Ryugin requires advance reservation months ahead; use a hotel concierge service for assistance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Shinjuku — begin at the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation decks (free entry) for sweeping city views including Mt. Fuji on clear April days. Explore Shinjuku's west side tech hub, including the NTT InterCommunication Center [ICC] — a cutting-edge museum dedicated to digital art and technology.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku's east side — wander through the atmospheric Golden Gai alleyways, visit Kabukicho's entertainment district, and discover the Isetan department store's legendary basement food hall (depachika) — a temple of Japanese culinary luxury featuring premium wagyu, artisan sweets, and rare regional delicacies.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Narisawa in Minami-Aoyama (short taxi from Shinjuku) — a two-Michelin-star restaurant by Chef Yoshihiro Narisawa, celebrated globally for 'Innovative Satoyama Cuisine' that bridges Japanese nature, sustainability, and avant-garde technique. Consistently ranked among Asia's and the world's best restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Premium café breakfast in Shinjuku — try a Japanese-style morning set at a traditional kissaten (coffee shop)
meals.lunch: Gourmet depachika lunch from Isetan's basement — curate your own premium bento from the finest stalls
meals.dinner: Two-Michelin-star innovative Japanese cuisine at Narisawa (approx. ¥35,000–¥55,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku is 30 minutes from Tsukiji by subway. The NTT ICC museum is a hidden gem for tech culture enthusiasts — check opening hours as it occasionally closes for installations. Narisawa requires advance reservation and is one of Japan's most sought-after dining experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Private cooking class experience — join a premium Tokyo cooking school for a hands-on session mastering sushi, ramen, or traditional Japanese home cooking (washoku). Classes taught by former professional chefs in a private kitchen setting, with market sourcing included.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nihonbashi — Tokyo's historic financial and cultural district, adjacent to Tsukiji. Visit the Coredo Muromachi complex for premium Japanese artisan goods, the Bank of Japan Currency Museum, and the Mitsukoshi flagship department store (Japan's oldest). Discover the underground art installations in the Nihonbashi waterway revival project.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-departure dinner (or celebratory mid-trip dinner) at a premium Nihonbashi restaurant. Try Nihonbashi Kakigaracho Sugita — a legendary, intimate sushi counter with a deeply traditional Edomae approach, or explore the refined French-Japanese cuisine at Quintessence.

meals.breakfast: Ingredients sourced during the morning cooking class — enjoy what you prepare as part of the experience
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a premium Nihonbashi café or the Mitsukoshi department store restaurant
meals.dinner: Premium Edomae sushi or French-Japanese dinner in Nihonbashi (approx. ¥25,000–¥50,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the private cooking class well in advance through services like Airbnb Experiences (premium tier) or dedicated Tokyo culinary schools such as Hattori Nutrition College's guest programs. Nihonbashi is a 10-minute walk from the Tsukiji hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Yanaka and Ueno — explore Yanaka Ginza, one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods. Wander through the atmospheric cemetery, artisan craft shops, and traditional shotengai (shopping street) for a glimpse of pre-modern Tokyo life and local food culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Ueno cultural complex — explore the Tokyo National Museum (Japan's largest and oldest museum, featuring extraordinary samurai artifacts and ancient technology), the National Museum of Nature and Science (with its Japan Pavilion on science and technology history), and stroll through Ueno Park if seasonal blooms remain.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Ueno or Akihabara — visit Kanda Yabu Soba, one of Tokyo's most historic and celebrated soba restaurants (founded 1880), for a refined traditional Japanese dinner. Alternatively, explore a premium izakaya in Ueno for a festive evening of small plates, sake, and Japanese whisky.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Street food lunch in Yanaka — grilled menchi katsu, handmade mochi, and artisan pickles from local vendors
meals.dinner: Historic soba counter or premium izakaya in Ueno/Kanda (approx. ¥8,000–¥20,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is approximately 35 minutes from Tsukiji by subway. The neighborhood is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. The Tokyo National Museum is closed on Mondays; Saturday is ideal. April may still offer late cherry blossoms in Ueno Park.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive private sake and Japanese whisky tasting experience — book a premium guided tasting session at a specialist sake bar or the Nikka Whisky bar in Tokyo. Learn about Japan's extraordinary fermentation traditions, regional sake varieties, and the global rise of Japanese whisky culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Marunouchi and Yurakucho districts — explore the premium retail and architectural landscape surrounding Tokyo Station. Visit the Kitte building (a beautifully converted historic post office with artisan food and craft shops), and the Intermediatheque museum — a stunning collaboration between Tokyo University and Japan Post featuring rare scientific and technological artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at a Tokyo landmark — dine at the Palace Hotel Tokyo's premier restaurant or the Mandarin Oriental Tokyo's Signature restaurant, both offering extraordinary Japanese and international cuisine with impeccable service and stunning city views. Celebrate the penultimate night with a premium Japanese whisky nightcap at a renowned bar such as Bar High Five in Ginza.

meals.breakfast: Luxurious hotel breakfast — full Japanese and Western spread
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at Kitte Marunouchi — explore the curated restaurant floors for the finest regional Japanese cuisine
meals.dinner: Landmark hotel fine dining experience (approx. ¥30,000–¥60,000 per person) followed by cocktails at Bar High Five

day_by_day.notes: Bar High Five in Ginza is one of the world's most celebrated cocktail bars — walk-in is possible but a reservation is recommended. The Intermediatheque museum is free to enter and a hidden gem for tech and science culture enthusiasts. Marunouchi is 15 minutes from Tsukiji by subway or taxi.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — revisit the Tsukiji Outer Market for one last fresh breakfast among the stalls. Purchase premium food souvenirs: high-grade dashi packs, artisan soy sauce, wasabi, premium green tea, and wagashi sweets. Explore any remaining neighborhood highlights near the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon at leisure — return to a favorite neighborhood or experience from the trip, complete any remaining shopping at Ginza or Nihonbashi for premium Japanese goods (lacquerware, ceramics, knives, electronics).
